summary.en: Represent text as character arrays, reserve a terminator, and distinguish literals from writable copies.
summary.bn: ক্যারেক্টার অ্যারেতে টেক্সট রাখো, শেষে null ক্যারেক্টার রাখো আর লিটারেল থেকে লেখা যায় এমন কপি আলাদা করো।

notes: Character arrays and null-terminated strings have the same central rules in C89 through C23. The examples use C17 and C99-style loop declarations. No newer standard makes a nonterminated character array acceptable to string-reading functions.

examples.title: Inspect the DIU characters
examples.explanationHtml: The indices 0, 1 and 2 hold D, I and U. Index 3 compares equal to the null character.

examples.title: Change a copy of a literal
examples.explanationHtml: room owns five writable char positions. Replacing index 3 changes its displayed name to Lab2.

examples.title: An early terminator hides a suffix
examples.explanationHtml: puts stops after ma. The later k remains stored, although it is outside the current string.

examples.title: A nonterminated array is not a string
examples.explanationHtml: The result is undefined: puts searches past the three valid elements for a null character. Add a fourth element containing '\0'.

practice.title: Measure a word without strlen
practice.statementHtml: Read one ASCII word of 1 to 80 bytes. Print Word: then its length on the next line. Count until the null character.
hints: The null character marks the stopping point.

practice.title: Print each character on its own line
practice.statementHtml: Read one ASCII word of 1 to 80 bytes. Print Word: then one character per line in original order.
hints: Use the element index to select one char.

practice.title: Keep a bounded prefix
practice.statementHtml: Read an ASCII word of 1 to 80 bytes and k from 0 to its length. Print Word and prefix length: then the first k characters as a string.
hints: Place the terminator at index k.

practice.title: Copy alternating characters
practice.statementHtml: Take a nonempty ASCII word no longer than 80 bytes. Print Word: then build a string from positions 0, 2, 4 and so on.
hints: Give the result its own null character.

quiz.prompt: How many char elements are needed to store "DIU" as a string?
quiz.explanation: Three letters need one additional element for the terminator.

quiz.prompt: What does '\0' represent at the end of a C string?
quiz.explanation: It is a stored zero character, separate from both the digit and the newline.

quiz.prompt: Which declaration creates a writable copy of Lab?
quiz.explanation: The array receives its own four elements; the pointer declarations refer to a literal.

quiz.prompt: What is the string length after setting label[0] = '\0'?
quiz.explanation: A zero at the first position represents an empty string in a valid array.

quiz.prompt: May char raw[3] = {'D', 'I', 'U'} be passed to puts?
options: Yes, puts knows the array length
quiz.explanation: puts needs a terminated string and does not receive the array bound.

quiz.prompt: Does a UTF-8 byte length always equal its visible letter count?
options: No, a letter may need multiple bytes
Yes, every char holds a letter
quiz.explanation: A char stores a byte; UTF-8 characters may span several bytes.

quiz.prompt: What does sizeof campus measure for char campus[] = "DIU" in its declaring scope?
options: The address of the first character
The four-element array size in bytes
quiz.explanation: The array contains the three letters and the zero terminator.

quiz.prompt: Which indexed characters and terminator check appear for campus?
quiz.explanation: The loop visits the three visible bytes before checking the fourth element.

quiz.prompt: What room name appears after changing room[3]?
quiz.explanation: The digit in the writable array changes while the earlier characters stay intact.

quiz.prompt: What remains visible after inserting a zero into marks?
quiz.explanation: The first null ends output without erasing the later array elements.

keyPoints.en: A C string ends at its first null character.
keyPoints.bn: C স্ট্রিং প্রথম null ক্যারেক্টারে শেষ হয়।

keyPoints.en: The literal "DIU" needs four char positions.
keyPoints.bn: "DIU" লিটারেলের জন্য চারটি ক্যারেক্টারের জায়গা লাগে।

keyPoints.en: An initialized char array holds a writable copy.
keyPoints.bn: শুরুতেই মান দেওয়া ক্যারেক্টার অ্যারেতে লেখা যায় এমন কপি থাকে।

keyPoints.en: Capacity includes space reserved for the terminator.
keyPoints.bn: বাফারের মোট জায়গার মধ্যে শেষের null ক্যারেক্টারও ধরতে হয়।

keyPoints.en: A byte count is not necessarily a count of visible letters.
keyPoints.bn: বাইটের সংখ্যা আর চোখে দেখা অক্ষরের সংখ্যা সব সময় এক নয়।

examQuestions.question: Draw the storage for char campus[] = "DIU" and distinguish length from capacity.
examQuestions.answerHtml: Four elements contain D, I, U and '\0'. The string length is three; capacity is four char elements. An early zero would shorten the string without resizing the array.

ma
suffix still stored: k

The first null ends output without erasing the later array elements.

examQuestions.question: Take a nonempty ASCII word no longer than 80 bytes. Print Word: then build a string from positions 0, 2, 4 and so on.
examQuestions.answerHtml:
#include <stdio.h>
#include <string.h>

int main(void)
{
    char text[81];
    puts("Word:");
    if (scanf("%80s", text) != 1) {
        return 1;
    }
    char result[81];
    size_t used = 0;
    for (size_t i = 0; text[i] != '\0'; i++) {
        if (i % 2 == 0) {
            result[used++] = text[i];
        }
    }
    result[used] = '\0';
    puts(result);
    return 0;
}

Give the result its own null character.
